q: During the progress of a reaction, an ____ intermediate is known as an activated complex. [2024 Local]
e: An activated complex is an unstable intermediate formed at the peak energy state during a chemical reaction.

q: Most chemical reactions react ____ at a high temperature than at a low temperature. [2025 Local]
e: Higher temperatures increase particle kinetic energy and collision frequency, speeding up the reaction.

q: A catalyst which is in the different phases of the reactants is ____ catalyst. [2026 Foreign]
e: A heterogeneous catalyst exists in a physical phase different from that of the reacting substances.

q: Reactions that are initiated by light are called ____ reactions. [2024 Local]
e: Photochemical reactions are initiated when reactant molecules absorb light energy.

q: Enzymes act as ____ for specific biochemical reactions in living systems. [2025 Local]
e: Enzymes function as natural biological catalysts that accelerate reactions in living organisms.

q: Enzymes are proteins that act as ____ for specific biochemical reactions. [2025 Local]
e: Enzymes are proteinaceous biocatalysts highly specific to individual biochemical reactions.

q: For a gaseous reaction, the rate of a reaction may be expressed in the unit, ____. [2025 Local]
e: Reaction rates in gas phase can be expressed in terms of concentration changes per unit time.

q: The reacting particles must collide with sufficient energy to form the ____ complex. [2025 Local]
e: Collision energy must meet or exceed activation energy to form the short-lived activated complex.

q: Candle wax burns only after the ____ of the candle is lighted. [2025 Local]
e: Lighting the wick provides the heat necessary to melt and vaporize the wax fuel.

q: The ____ theory can explain the effect of concentration on the rate of reaction. [2025 Local]
e: Collision theory explains how reactant particle concentration impacts effective collision rate.

q: A hydrogen molecule and an iodine molecule collide to form an ____ intermediate [H₂I₂] which exists for a short time. [2025 Local]
e: The activated complex [H₂I₂] is an unstable transition state before forming product HI molecules.

q: The effect of concentration on the rate of reaction can be explained by the ____. [2025 Local]
e: Collision theory accounts for changes in reaction rate based on particle collision frequency.

q: Transition state is a highly ____ state that would be highly unstable. [2025 Local]
e: The transition state corresponds to the maximum energy barrier on the reaction path.

q: ____ units are used if the reactant or product is in solution. [2025 Local]
e: For reactions in solution, rates are measured using concentration terms like moles per unit volume per time.

q: If higher the concentration of reactant will be used up, the rate of reaction will be ____. [2025 Local]
e: Greater reactant concentration increases particle collisions, leading to a faster overall reaction rate.

q: When the reactant molecules absorb the light (hν), a ____ reaction takes place. [2026 Foreign]
e: Absorption of light photons (hν) drives photo-initiated chemical transformations.

q: The catalyst will speed up the production and this has helped reduce the ____ requirements. [2025 Local]
e: Catalysts lower the activation energy, decreasing energy consumption in industrial reactions.

q: Rate of a reaction is measured in terms of the change in amount of a reactant or a product per unit of ____. [2025 Local]
e: Reaction rate defines how quickly reactant amounts decrease or product amounts increase over time.

q: White phosphorus bursts into flames when exposed to ____. [2025 Local]
e: White phosphorus is highly reactive and undergoes spontaneous combustion when exposed to atmospheric air.

q: The volume of hydrogen gas released in the process of reaction at time intervals can be measured by ____ method. [2025 Local]
e: A gas syringe setup accurately collects and measures evolved gas volume at set time intervals.

q: The rate of reaction depends on the rate of successful ____ between reactant particles. [2026 Foreign]
e: Only collisions with appropriate orientation and sufficient energy successfully convert reactants into products.

q: According to the collision theory, a reaction will speed up if the ____ of collision increases. [2026 Foreign]
e: Increasing collision frequency per unit time raises the number of effective collisions.

q: The catalyst that decreases the rate of a reaction is known as ____ catalyst. [2026 Foreign]
e: A negative catalyst or inhibitor slows down reaction rates by raising the required energy pathway.
